# jamfplatform_pro_static_computer_group (Data Source)

Use this only when the group must belong to a Jamf Pro site. For everything else prefer `jamfplatform_device_group` with `device_type = "computer"` and `group_type = "static"`, which manages the same computer group across Jamf Platform and is the supported path; it has no site attribute, which is the one thing this adds.

Looks one group up by `id` or by exact `name`, and reports the computers in it. Supply exactly one of the two.

**Required Jamf permissions**

Jamf lists this under **Platform environment** scope (preferred for new integrations) or **Tenant** scope. You choose an integration's scope when you create it in Jamf Account, and cannot change it afterwards. The provider names the scopes it accepts when you configure it, and for a few families that is wider than Jamf lists here. Grant the API integration the following permissions in Jamf Account — see [Getting started with the Platform API](https://developer.jamf.com/platform-api/reference/getting-started-with-platform-api). `Category` and `Permission` name the section and row of the permission picker; `Actions` are the boxes to tick within that row.

| Category | Permission | Actions | API capability |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inventory | Device groups | Read | `device-groups` |

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "jamfplatform_pro_static_computer_group" "example_by_id" {
  id = "41"
}

data "jamfplatform_pro_static_computer_group" "example_by_name" {
  name = "Design Macs"
}

# The computers in the group, which only the singular lookup reports.
output "design_macs_members" {
  value = data.jamfplatform_pro_static_computer_group.example_by_name.assigned_computer_ids
}

output "static_computer_group_example_by_id" {
  value = data.jamfplatform_pro_static_computer_group.example_by_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Jamf Pro identifier for the group. Mutually exclusive with `name`.
- `name` (String) Group name, matched exactly. Mutually exclusive with `id`.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `assigned_computer_ids` (Set of String) Jamf Pro identifiers of the computers in the group.
- `description` (String) Note Jamf Pro keeps with the group.
- `platform_id` (String) Identifier for this group across Jamf Platform, for targeting it from a blueprint, a compliance benchmark, or any `jamfplatform_device_*` construct that asks for a group.
- `site_id` (String) Jamf Pro site the group belongs to. `-1` means no site.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
